title: Rabbi Chalafta ben Shaul
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud: Berakhot ch. 1 halakhah 5, folio 10a; Peah ch. 2 end of halakhah 4; Maaserot ch. 2 end of halakhah 3; Terumot ch. 10 halakhah 6; Bikkurim ch. 2 halakhah 1 (and cited in Midrash Tehillim 26:7); Shabbat ch. 4 halakhah 2; Moed Katan ch. 1 beginning of halakhah 9. In all of them the wording is "Rabbi Chalafta ben Shaul recited." From this Hyman infers that he was among the reciters of baraitot. Hyman considers his name in the Bavli corrupted to Rabbi Tachlifa, as in Moed Katan 10a: "But Rabbi Tachlifa bar Shaul recited: and they agree that one does not twist [ropes]"; and in Dikdukei Soferim the reading is Rabbi Chalafta ben Shaul. And in Zevachim 93b: "For it was taught: Rabbi Tachlifa bar Shaul says" — two errors occurred there: (a) that he was not a tanna of the Mishnaic period, and it should read "Rabbi ... recited" etc., as the statement is cited in Menachot 7a; (b) that it should read Rabbi Chalafta ben Shaul, as in the reading of Dikdukei Soferim.

Likewise in Megillah 23a, "Rabbi Tachlifa bar Shmuel recited" should read, as in Dikdukei Soferim, Rabbi Chalafta bar Shaul. He is mentioned in Berakhot 29a, where they said: "These seven [blessings] of Shabbat correspond to what? Rabbi Chalafta ben Shaul said: Corresponding to the seven voices that David said over the waters," etc.

notes.text: Hyman first characterizes him as a reciter of baraitot, then denies that the disputed formula should place him among the tannaim of the Mishnaic period. His preferred Chalafta/Tachlifa and Shaul/Shmuel readings remain attributed textual judgments.

The inspected Moed Katan 10a reads Rav Tachlifa bar Shaul reciting the rope-twisting rule. Hyman prefers Chalafta and distinguishes the reciter formula from the disputed tannaitic formula. The exact Dikdukei Soferim readings were not inspected; neither a baraita reciter nor this occurrence automatically establishes a Mishnaic-era identity.
